bond_price_cents discounts each event by (1 + y) ** (t - 1), one period short.
bond_price_cents warns (a UserWarning) at a negative yield, a valid input.
bond_price_cents reads yield_bps as a percentage, so the per-period yield is 100 times too large.
Bond.events returns the periods in descending order, although the page says the list is sorted by period.
Bond.events adds a zero-amount event in period 0 (the trade date), which the page says no event falls in.
Bond.events adds the face to the stored last event each time it is called, so a second call differs from the first.
bond_price_cents truncates the exact present value toward zero instead of rounding it half away from zero.

Student error: Bond.events prints a line when the coupon is zero, a valid input, which the page's silence rule forbids.

CashTrade accepts price_cents = -1, an off-by-one on the boundary the page names as refused.
CashTrade accepts settlement_day = 0 (period 0 is the trade date), which the page names as refused.
A sale is booked as a payment, because the side enters the cash flow as an absolute value.
Each coupon is the difference of cumulative rounded accruals, so coupons differ by a cent from face times rate.
The last event (its coupon and the face together) is priced undiscounted, selected by amount > face.
Bond accepts a negative face_cents (checks only abs(face) against zero).
Bond accepts periods = -1 (checks only abs(periods) against 1).
CashTrade accepts quantity = -1 (checks only abs(quantity) against 1).

bond_price_cents accepts yield_bps = -10000, so 1 + y is zero and the division fails.

The per-period yield is halved before discounting, as if it were a semiannual rate applied per period.
Discounts each event with (1 - y) instead of (1 + y), so the sign of the yield is reversed.

Off-by-one on the coupon schedule: the final period pays the face and no coupon.
